claim: The region the Rigvedic fort passages refer to contained fortified sites.
claim_class: ANCIENT — a claim about the material record of a region in a period
locator: Owner instruction to this session, 2026-09-08, commissioning BF-027 and BF-028. No source was named with it and none is asserted here.
notes: ENTERS UNVERIFIED AND STAYS THERE. CLAUDE.md: promotion requires a retrieval event logged in the access ledger; argument does not promote a claim and confidence does not promote a claim. This unit retrieved the published site (SRC-099) and nothing else - no excavation report, no site gazetteer, no survey. Not resolved, per the commissioning instruction. WHAT THE CLAIM STILL NEEDS BEFORE IT CAN BE TESTED, and the reason it is not testable as worded: every one of its four terms is unbounded. (1) WHICH REGION - the page argues the Sarasvati-Sindhu and the northwest from its own river counts (dasa-forts-rigveda.html:426-431); "the region referred to" is not established, it is one of the things in dispute. (2) WHEN - a fortified site in the region at 2600 BCE, at 1700 BCE and at 1000 BCE bear on the Rigvedic passages quite differently, and the date range is exactly what BF-027 finds unsettled. (3) WHAT COUNTS AS FORTIFIED - constitution section 7 names "fort" as an inherited English category requiring audit, and this repository has already run part of that audit: Grassmann glosses pur- "wall of stones and clay, entrenchment, palisade", not city, not fortress (CORRECTIONS-PENDING.md section 3.4), and BF-017 logs "fort" as a default gloss that was let stand. A perimeter wall, a mud-brick enclosure and a monumental concentric fortress are three claims. (4) HOW MANY, and whether "contained fortified sites" is meant to bear on the identification at all. NOTE, because it changes what work is owed: this position is not new to the site. dasa-forts-rigveda.html already asserts it, unsourced, at :432 ("Late Harappan and post-urban settlements persisted in this region, and they are the only candidates the chronology permits") and in its candidate table at :444-447 ("Post-urban Harappan settlements | Cemetery H, Late Harappan sites in Punjab and Haryana | Contemporary with the family books. Settled, walled, and in the right place"). So the owner position and the published page agree - and neither is sourced. Registering it as INHERITED-UNVERIFIED makes visible that a claim already in public copy has no retrieval behind it. Queued as RQ-D-01.

claim: The identification of the Rigvedic forts with Indus-civilisation sites has been institutionally dismissed rather than evidentially refuted.
claim_class: HISTORIOGRAPHICAL — a claim about the conduct and standing of a scholarly literature, not about antiquity
locator: Owner instruction to this session, 2026-09-08, commissioning BF-027 and BF-028. No source was named with it and none is asserted here.
notes: ENTERS UNVERIFIED AND STAYS THERE, on the same rule as DFO-001. Not resolved, per the commissioning instruction. REGISTERED SEPARATELY AND NOT MERGED WITH DFO-001, and the separation is the load-bearing act, not a filing convenience. This claim is not about forts, the Indus, the Rigveda or the second millennium BCE. It is about a literature: what its authors did, on what grounds, and whether a position left it by refutation or by attrition. It could be entirely true while DFO-001 is false, and entirely false while DFO-001 is true. The link between them is a separate claim and is typed at BR-F-001 in 03-REGISTERS/CROSS-DOMAIN-BRIDGES.csv; nothing may be inferred from one to the other except through that row. THIS IS ALSO AN ARGUMENT FROM ABSENCE and constitution section 6 governs it: the absence asserted is the absence of an evidential refutation. Section 6 requires the absence to be characterised before it is argued from, and then typed as one of NOT PRODUCED, NOT PRESERVED, NOT EXCAVATED, NOT PUBLISHED, NOT ACCESSIBLE, NOT RECOGNIZED, DOCUMENTED DESTRUCTION or ABSENT DESPITE ADEQUATE SEARCH. It is UNTYPED here and cannot be typed without a literature search this unit did not run; the section 6 worksheet - what a refutation would look like, where it would have been published, and whether we could recognise one - is set out in 04-AUDITS/dasa-forts-mohenjo-method.md section 4. Until that search is run the claim is not merely unverified, it is unformed: "no refutation was published" and "a refutation was published and we have not read it" are indistinguishable from where this repository stands. METHOD STEP 11 IS THE INSTRUMENT, not step 6, and the distinction matters for what work is owed. Step 11 asks a position to be placed as historically influential, currently supported, revised, disputed, held by citation inertia, abandoned or rejected. "Abandoned" and "rejected" are different verdicts and this claim asserts the first against the second; a step-11 standing audit could settle it, and no step-11 audit of this literature exists in this repository. The named position to trace first is Parpola's, which dasa-forts-rigveda.html:441 already cites in the opposite direction ("Parpola argued explicitly that the Dasa forts are BMAC"). BOTH ADVERSARIAL TESTS BEAR ON THIS ROW AND ARE LOGGED IN THE METHOD NOTE SECTION 5. The preferred-counter-narrative challenge is the live one: "dismissed, not refuted" is the standard form of an appeal against a scholarly consensus, it is available for free to any position that has lost an argument, and it is correct often enough - constitution section 4V and the archive audit exist because institutional power does shape what gets recorded and refuted - that it cannot be waved away either. It is registered at the same status as DFO-001, given no rhetorical advantage from being anti-institutional, and given no rhetorical penalty for it either. Queued as RQ-D-02.
